title: Registered FULL with a passed clippy stage (and an unrun docs stage) gets no native verification: "unclassified_stages ... clippy, docs"
outcome: A registered committed-input FULL whose stages TermAl does not classify (for example Engram's clippy and docs) either earns the native verification its recognized stages support, or is refused with a reason that names the exact stage and the correction. An unrecognized or unrun stage never silently withholds credit for the whole run without a defined rule.
acceptance: The stage classification that produced "unclassified_stages: completed run has no recognized check for clippy, docs; native verification was not granted" is located by file and line, and the rule for unrecognized and for not-run stages is stated in the item note.

Clippy (cargo clippy ... -D warnings) is recognized as a lint-kind check, consistent with Greg's ruling that clippy must not block a check-in (2026-11-16): a passed clippy stage counts as lint evidence, and a clippy stage is not required for test or build credit. A docs stage that did not run neither grants nor blocks test or build credit; its absence is reported, not fatal. Shown by behavioural tests over a completed run with those stages.
The independent review pair has no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and the full gate passes on the exact landed input.
